  "H1": {
    "name": "Latent State Abstraction Hypothesis",
    "mechanism": "The embodied world model functions primarily as a high-dimensional latent state estimator that compresses sensory inputs into a compact, task-agnostic representation. The 'world model' is not a generative simulator of physics, but a predictive encoder that minimizes reconstruction error in latent space. Success depends on the dimensionality of the latent space matching the intrinsic dimensionality of the environment's dynamics.",
    "observable_predictions": [
      "Performance on downstream control tasks will degrade non-linearly as the latent dimensionality deviates from the estimated intrinsic dimensionality of the environment.",
      "The latent representations will exhibit high mutual information with the true physical state variables (e.g., position, velocity) but low correlation with high-frequency sensory noise.",
      "Interventions that increase the complexity of the latent space (e.g., adding unnecessary parameters) will lead to overfitting and reduced generalization to novel environments."
    ],
    "falsification_conditions": [
      "If a model with a significantly higher latent dimensionality than the intrinsic dimensionality of the environment achieves equal or better performance on novel tasks, H1 is falsified.",
      "If the latent representations show no significant correlation with ground-truth physical state variables (e.g., via probing classifiers) while maintaining high task performance, H1 is falsified.",
      "If performance remains stable or improves when the latent space is artificially constrained below the intrinsic dimensionality, H1 is falsified."
    ]
  },
  "H2": {
    "name": "Causal Graphical Structure Hypothesis",
    "mechanism": "The embodied world model explicitly learns a causal graphical model (DAG) of the environment. The 'world model' is a structural causal model that captures the directed dependencies between variables. Success depends on the accuracy of the learned causal edges, not just predictive accuracy. The model uses this structure for counterfactual reasoning and robust planning.",
    "observable_predictions": [
      "The model will exhibit superior performance in counterfactual scenarios (e.g., 'what if I had not moved?') compared to models that only learn predictive correlations.",
      "The learned causal graph will align with the ground-truth causal structure of the environment (e.g., verified via intervention experiments).",
      "The model will be robust to distributional shifts that preserve the causal structure but change the marginal distributions of variables."
    ],
    "falsification_conditions": [
      "If the model fails to perform counterfactual reasoning tasks (e.g., predicting outcomes of unobserved interventions) while maintaining high predictive accuracy, H2 is falsified.",
      "If the learned causal graph (extracted via interpretability tools) does not match the ground-truth causal structure, H2 is falsified.",
      "If the model's performance degrades significantly under distributional shifts that preserve causal structure but change marginals, H2 is falsified."
    ]
  },
  "H3": {
    "name": "Predictive Energy Landscape Hypothesis",
    "mechanism": "The embodied world model operates as a predictive energy-based model (EBM) that defines an energy function over state-action sequences. The 'world model' is a potential field where low-energy states correspond to likely future trajectories. Success depends on the smoothness and accuracy of the energy landscape, not on explicit state estimation or causal structure. The model navigates this landscape to plan actions.",
    "observable_predictions": [
      "The model will exhibit smooth, continuous changes in predicted outcomes as actions are varied slightly, reflecting the smoothness of the energy landscape.",
      "The model will be able to identify multiple local minima in the energy landscape, corresponding to different plausible future trajectories.",
      "The model will be robust to noise in sensory inputs, as the energy function integrates over uncertainty."
    ],
    "falsification_conditions": [
      "If the model exhibits discontinuous or erratic changes in predicted outcomes for small changes in actions, H3 is falsified.",
      "If the model fails to identify multiple plausible future trajectories (local minima) in environments with multiple valid outcomes, H3 is falsified.",
      "If the model's performance degrades significantly under high sensory noise, H3 is falsified."
    ]
  },
  "H0": {
    "name": "Null Hypothesis: No Distinct World Model Mechanism",
    "mechanism": "The observed performance of 'embodied world models' is not due to a distinct world model mechanism (latent abstraction, causal structure, or energy landscape) but is entirely attributable to the general capacity of the underlying neural network architecture (e.g., transformer, RNN) to fit complex input-output mappings. The 'world model' is an emergent property of over-parameterization and large-scale training, not a specific architectural or algorithmic component.",
    "observable_predictions": [
      "A standard neural network without any explicit world model components (e.g., no latent space, no causal structure, no energy function) will achieve comparable performance on embodied tasks if given sufficient capacity and data.",
      "The performance of the 'world model' will scale with the number of parameters in the underlying network, independent of any specific world model architecture.",
      "The 'world model' will not exhibit any specific interpretability features (e.g., latent states, causal graphs, energy landscapes) that are distinct from the general activations of the underlying network."
